Are proofs written in prose with displayed steps, or do they hand-wave / assert conclusions? Does it end with a position/status statement (what's settled, what's open)? Does it have its own bibliography of primary literature at the end?

House-style violations — this repo's own manuscript style FORBIDS: any internal file paths, branch names, theorem/lemma identifiers from a Lean codebase, module names, or any narration of "what was wrong before" or the process of writing/fixing the paper (no dev-narrative). 5. LaTeX health: unmatched braces/environments, undefined \ref or \cite targets, package issues, anything that would likely fail to compile with xelatex.
6. For iutt_fully_conventional.tex: note the title, abstract wording, and any date/version markers, since there is a second file `iutt.tex` in the same directory that another reviewer is checking separately — just flag if this file's content or title suggests it's an earlier/alternate/duplicate draft of the same result (don't read the other file yourself, just note anything relevant from this file's own internal cues).

73	\title{\bfseries Inter-Universal Teichm\"uller Theory\\\large A Paraconsistent Formulation in Conventional Mathematical Notation}
74	\author{Lando Mills}
75	\date{}
76	
77	\begin{document}
78	\maketitle
79	
80	\begin{abstract}
81	The construction is formulated on the sixteen-state space
82	\[
83	\mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}),
84	\]
85	with a non-explosive consequence relation.  This is a rebase of the logical
86	substrate, not a reinterpretation of a prior Boolean construction.  The
87	Belnap--Dunn four-state system is the $t,f$-free subspace of $\mathcal X$, and
88	$\{F,T\}$ is a further lossy restriction.
89	
90	The mathematical operations needed below are ordinary maps on this state
91	space and on enriched spaces built over it: projections $\pi_T,\pi_F$, the
92	involution $\nu$, decompositions $\delta_n$, recombinations $\mu_n$, an
93	information extension $\eta$, context maps $f$ and $\ell$, a fixation map
94	$\kappa$, and a terminal scalar functional $h$.  Inter-Universal Teichm\"uller Theory is
95	then described by compositions and branch diagrams built from these maps.
96	The $\Theta$-link transports arithmetic data without identifying the ring
97	structures on its two sides; the log-$\Theta$ construction retains filtration
98	position; and the bounded-discrepancy calculation terminates at
99	\[
100	Ftf=\{F,t,f\}
101	\]
102	while its reconnection condition holds.  Cyclic phase is represented by the
103	standard action of $C_{12}$ on a twelve-position presentation.  Scholze--Stix
104	obtain a vacuous scalar inequality only after suppressing the filtration index
105	carrying the $j^2$ weights.  Mochizuki correctly rejects their commuting-loop
106	surrogate, but the stronger point is that local incompatibility is admissible
107	and non-explosive once locality and filtration position have been retained.
108	Classicalization therefore occurs only as a downstream projection of the
109	calculation.
110	\end{abstract}
111	
112	\section{Rebasing the logical substrate}
113	\label{sec:rebasing}
114	
115	The logical base used in this paper is constitutive.  It is not an optional
116	semantic gloss on a construction that is first completed in a classical
117	two-valued universe.
118	
119	A \emph{reinterpretation} leaves the underlying consequence relation and
120	admissible carrier unchanged and assigns a new description to objects already
121	formed there.  That is not the operation performed here.  The present
122	construction is \emph{rebased}: formulas, graph states, closure predicates,
123	contradictory states, filtrations, cyclic phases, and terminal readouts are
124	formed directly in the non-explosive carrier and are governed from the outset
125	by its consequence relation.
126	
127	Concretely, the base is
128	\[
129	  \mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}),
130	\]
131	together with the directed graph operations introduced below and a consequence
132	relation for which local contradiction does not entail an arbitrary conclusion:
133	\[
134	  p,\neg p\nvdash q
135	\]
136	for unrelated $q$.  States such as
137	\[
138	  A=\{T,F,t,f\},
139	  \qquad
140	  Ftf=\{F,t,f\},
141	\]
142	are therefore values of the calculation itself.  They are not annotations
143	attached after a classical computation has already finished.
144	
145	The Boolean pair
146	\[
147	  B_4=\{F,T\}
148	\]
149	appears only as a proper downstream restriction.  Classicalization is a map
150	\[
151	  \clproj:\mathcal X\longrightarrow B_4
152	\]
153	that forgets carrier information.  Hence the logical direction of the paper is
154	\[
155	  \boxed{\text{full nonclassical calculation}}
156	  \;\longrightarrow\;
157	  \boxed{\text{downstream Boolean shadow}},
158	\]
159	never the reverse.  In particular, a scalar terminal inequality may lie in a
160	classical codomain without implying that the calculation which produced it was
161	classical.
162

187	The full carrier and the Boolean restriction are not equivalent descriptions

190	contradictory fixed point as a Boolean state.
191	\end{proposition}

195	\[
196	  \clproj(\{F\})=\clproj(\{F,t,f\})=F.

199	\[
200	  \Inc(B)=B,

203	Thus classicalization loses states and operations that are native to the
204	calculation.  It cannot be an invertible change of description.
205	\end{proof}

361	\section{FOUR inside the full carrier}

363	The full carrier contains the Belnap--Dunn FOUR slice
364	\[

368	falsity only, and $B$ carries both.  Negation fixes the two nonclassical states,
369	\[
370	\neg N=N,\qquad \neg B=B,
371	\]
372	and exchanges the classical poles $T$ and $F$.  The crucial point is not simply
373	that FOUR has two additional labels.  It allows incompatible information to
374	remain present without identifying that state with arbitrary consequence
375	\cite{belnap,dunn,uno}.

384	\[
385	F <_{t} N <_{t} T,
386	\qquad
387	F <_{t} B <_{t} T,
388	\]
389	with $N$ and $B$ incomparable.  The same carrier therefore supports different
390	motions without forcing one motion to erase the others.  Contradiction is the
391	top of information, not a detonation command.

531	\section{IUT: incompatible transport retained}
532	
533	IUT begins with initial $\Theta$-data attached to an elliptic curve over a number
534	field and constructs Hodge theaters carrying arithmetic and geometric data
535	\cite{iut1}.  The point relevant here is the relation between theaters.  The
536	$\Theta$-link relates Frobenioid-theoretic portions of one theater to another in
537	a manner that is deliberately not compatible with the respective ring/scheme
538	structures.  The ring structures on the two sides are not transported as one
539	ring structure.  The theory works instead with what it calls an \emph{alien ring
540	structure}: one side is described from the standpoint of a structure that is not
541	its own.
542	
543	That is already a paraconsistent situation.  The link does not need to say that
544	one ring structure is secretly the other.  It needs to retain enough of both for
545	a meaningful comparison to survive their incompatibility.  The information is
546	therefore not exhausted by either classical pole.  If one insists that every
547	carrier state be reduced to exactly $T$ or exactly $F$, the alien part of the
548	alien ring structure has been removed before the transport runs.
549	
550	The same pattern persists in the three indeterminacies.  They are not a temporary
551	failure to identify the unique classical object that ``really'' exists.  They
552	are controlled latitude in the transport itself.  Some data are retained only
553	up to automorphism, unit action, or upper semi-compatibility.  The relevant
554	question is consequently not ``which side wins?'' but ``what is invariant while
555	incompatible or incomplete determinations remain live?''  That is the ordinary
556	question of a paraconsistent information order.

558	The familiar cartoon of the alien ring structure makes the point sharply.  Take
559	two copies $\mathbb R_0$ and $\mathbb R_1$ and glue them by a bijection that is

667	\section{Indeterminacy without erasure}
668	
669	IUT's three indeterminacies are often described as the price paid for comparing
670	objects across alien structures.  They delimit the live
671	variation directly: they delimit which information is fixed and which information is
672	allowed to vary without destroying the transport.
673	
674	An underdetermined state has the shape of $N$: neither classical determination
675	has yet been supplied.  An overdetermined state has the shape of $B$: both are
676	present.  These need not be globally assigned labels once and for all.  The same
677	construction can move through regions of incompleteness and regions of
678	inconsistency.  The important invariant is that neither state triggers
679	explosion, so local indeterminacy does not license arbitrary conclusions about
680	unrelated parts of the graph.
681	
682	This is why the classical restriction is not merely inconvenient.  Its two
683	canonical collapse maps identify both $N$ and $B$ with a classical pole:
684	\[
685	r(N)=r(B)=T,
686	\qquad
687	c(N)=c(B)=F.
688	\]
689	Thus incompleteness and inconsistency become indistinguishable after either
690	collapse.  IUT, by contrast, repeatedly depends on knowing what survives under a
691	specified indeterminacy.  A carrier restriction that erases the distinction between
692	``not yet determined'' and ``jointly but incompatibly determined'' cannot serve
693	as the carrier for that bookkeeping.

695	\section{Conjugate synchronization as preserved multiplicity}
696	
697	Conjugate synchronization aligns copies of the local Galois group across labels
698	so that theta evaluation can be made without introducing the conjugacy
699	indeterminacy that would otherwise obstruct the comparison.  It does not make
700	the labels one label.  It makes a family jointly readable while preserving the
701	fact that it is a family.
702	
703	Synchronization retains multiplicity.  It does not require the
704	carrier to contract all copies to one classical representative.  It requires a
705	common relation that can be carried across several simultaneously present
706	copies.  In carrier language the useful state is therefore not ``one lane has
707	won'' but ``the lanes have acquired a common image.''  The all-lane state $A$
708	is an extreme example of that phenomenon: every base atom is present in one
709	carrier state without that state becoming trivial.
710	
711	The distinction matters because $A$ is not the statement that every proposition
712	is derivable.  It is one value of one carrier at one point in one graph.  Local
713	saturation of information is not global logical explosion.

715	\section{Frobenius-like and \texorpdfstring{\'etale}{etale}-like motion}
716	
717	IUT repeatedly contrasts Frobenius-like, order-conscious constructions with
718	\'etale-like structures in which certain ordering information has been forgotten
719	or made permutation-invariant \cite{iut1,iut2}.  The full carrier carries this contrast because the same carrier supports more than one
720	order.  Nothing requires us to identify a particular IUT axis once and for all
721	with a particular lattice order.  The stronger and safer claim is structural:
722	IUT needs simultaneous order-sensitive and order-insensitive descriptions of
723	related data, while a bilattice/trilattice carrier is built precisely to let one
724	state participate in several orderings without being duplicated into separate
725	worlds.
726	
727	This matters for the $\Theta$-link and Log-link.  A horizontal or vertical move
728	in the log-theta-lattice changes what is being transported or forgotten, but it
729	does not require a new logical universe.  The same value can be compared under another
730	order without leaving the carrier.  The noncommutativity of
731	moves is then allowed to remain noncommutative.  There is no requirement that two
732	paths through the lattice collapse to a single Boolean equality before the
733	result can be meaningful.

735	\section{Paper I: the theater is already non-Boolean}
736	
737	Paper I constructs the Hodge theaters and the links among them \cite{iut1}.  Its
738	central act is not the production of a globally shared ring structure.  It is
739	the controlled passage among structures after precisely such a shared ring
740	structure has been relinquished.
741	
742	The geometric and arithmetic symmetries of the labels coexist inside a theater.
743	The $\Theta$-link then passes from one theater to another through structures that
744	are sufficiently stripped of ring rigidity to admit the link.  What survives is
745	not an equality of ringed spaces but a package of invariants that can be
746	recognized on both sides.  The alien ring structure is therefore not an
747	exception occurring after a classical construction.  It is the condition that
748	makes the inter-universal movement possible.
749	
750	Paper I establishes a carrier large enough for mutually
751	alien determinations to remain simultaneously addressable.  The mono-analytic
752	core is valuable not because it secretly reconstructs one common classical
753	ring, but because it identifies content that survives when the surrounding ring
754	structures do not coincide.  This is the same informational logic expressed by
755	FOUR: keep the information that is jointly supported, keep track of what is
756	missing or incompatible, and do not infer everything from the incompatibility.
757	
758	\subsection{Chains of theaters}
759	
760	The chain of $\Theta$-Hodge theaters is especially clear in this execution.  Each
761	link is a transport step whose admissibility depends on forgetting enough local
762	structure to move and retaining enough invariant structure to recognize the
763	result.  The chain does not become meaningful by restoring a single global ring
764	at every step.  It becomes meaningful because each step has a controlled
765	interface.
766	
767	This is exactly the role of unfilled ports in a directed graph.  An unfilled port is not an
768	error; it is a living end, a place where another component can bind.  A theater
769	that exposes only the structure needed for the next link behaves like a
770	component with a typed living end.  Completion is not demanded prematurely.
771	
772	\section{Paper II: evaluation across alien descriptions}
773	
774	Paper II develops the Hodge--Arakelov-theoretic evaluation and the Kummer theory
775	relating Frobenius-like and Galois-theoretic forms of the theta data
776	\cite{iut2}.  The crucial operation is not the elimination of multiplicity but
777	the ability to evaluate coherently across it.
778	
779	Multiradiality is an information-preserving change
780	of viewpoint.  A uniradial description is tied to one spoke; a multiradial
781	description can speak from several spokes.  What must remain fixed is the coric
782	content that survives these shifts.  The indeterminacies specify which changes
783	of representation are tolerated.  They do not designate noise to be thrown
784	away.
785	
786	Cyclotomic, discrete, and constant-multiple rigidities are useful precisely
787	because they survive the admissible spread.  A rigidity is an invariant under
788	the relevant movement.  In the carrier, there is content
789	that survives even while other atoms are added, swapped, projected, or held in
790	contradictory combination.  Information growth around an invariant is not the
791	same as loss of the invariant.
792	
793	The Gaussian Frobenioid constructions sharpen the point.  The theory can pass
794	between Frobenius-like and \`etale-like presentations of theta values without
795	requiring the two presentations to be literally identical structures.  Their
796	relation is carried by Kummer theory and the stated invariants.  The carrier retains the relation itself, not merely its two endpoints.
797	
798	\section{Paper III: the log-theta-lattice in motion}

801	the log-theta-lattice \cite{iut3}.  Horizontal and vertical transports coexist.
802	The log-link and the theta-related links do not need to commute into one classical
803	identity to be usable.  Their difference is part of the geometry of the lattice.

\begin{abstract}
The construction is formulated on the sixteen-state space
\[
\mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}),
\]
with a non-explosive consequence relation.  This is a rebase of the logical
substrate, not a reinterpretation of a prior Boolean construction.  The
Belnap--Dunn four-state system is the $t,f$-free subspace of $\mathcal X$, and
$\{F,T\}$ is a further lossy restriction.

The mathematical operations needed below are ordinary maps on this state
space and on enriched spaces built over it: projections $\pi_T,\pi_F$, the
involution $\nu$, decompositions $\delta_n$, recombinations $\mu_n$, an
information extension $\eta$, context maps $f$ and $\ell$, a fixation map
$\kappa$, and a terminal scalar functional $h$.  Inter-Universal Teichm\"uller Theory is
then described by compositions and branch diagrams built from these maps.
The $\Theta$-link transports arithmetic data without identifying the ring
structures on its two sides; the log-$\Theta$ construction retains filtration
position; and the bounded-discrepancy calculation terminates at
\[
Ftf=\{F,t,f\}
\]
while its reconnection condition holds.  Cyclic phase is represented by the
standard action of $C_{12}$ on a twelve-position presentation.  Scholze--Stix
obtain a vacuous scalar inequality only after suppressing the filtration index
carrying the $j^2$ weights.  Mochizuki correctly rejects their commuting-loop
surrogate, but the stronger point is that local incompatibility is admissible
and non-explosive once locality and filtration position have been retained.
Classicalization therefore occurs only as a downstream projection of the
calculation.
\end{abstract}

\section{Rebasing the logical substrate}
\label{sec:rebasing}

The logical base used in this paper is constitutive.  It is not an optional
semantic gloss on a construction that is first completed in a classical
two-valued universe.

A \emph{reinterpretation} leaves the underlying consequence relation and
admissible carrier unchanged and assigns a new description to objects already
formed there.  That is not the operation performed here.  The present
construction is \emph{rebased}: formulas, graph states, closure predicates,
contradictory states, filtrations, cyclic phases, and terminal readouts are
formed directly in the non-explosive carrier and are governed from the outset
by its consequence relation.

Concretely, the base is
\[
  \mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}),
\]
together with the directed graph operations introduced below and a consequence
relation for which local contradiction does not entail an arbitrary conclusion:
\[
  p,\neg p\nvdash q
\]
for unrelated $q$.  States such as
\[
  A=\{T,F,t,f\},
  \qquad
  Ftf=\{F,t,f\},
\]
are therefore values of the calculation itself.  They are not annotations
attached after a classical computation has already finished.

The Boolean pair
\[
  B_4=\{F,T\}
\]
appears only as a proper downstream restriction.  Classicalization is a map
\[
  \clproj:\mathcal X\longrightarrow B_4
\]
that forgets carrier information.  Hence the logical direction of the paper is
\[
  \boxed{\text{full nonclassical calculation}}
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \boxed{\text{downstream Boolean shadow}},
\]
never the reverse.  In particular, a scalar terminal inequality may lie in a
classical codomain without implying that the calculation which produced it was
classical.

\begin{proposition}[The rebase is not a re-description]
The full carrier and the Boolean restriction are not equivalent descriptions
of the same logical state space.  In particular, the classicalization map
$\clproj:\mathcal X\to B_4$ is non-injective and cannot preserve the
contradictory fixed point as a Boolean state.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Distinct full-carrier states have the same Boolean shadow; for example,
\[
  \clproj(\{F\})=\clproj(\{F,t,f\})=F.
\]
Moreover the contradictory state $B=\{T,F\}$ is fixed by information closure,
\[
  \Inc(B)=B,
\]
whereas every map into $B_4=\{F,T\}$ must return one of the two Boolean poles.
Thus classicalization loses states and operations that are native to the
calculation.  It cannot be an invertible change of description.
\end{proof}

This distinction governs every later section.  Transport without
ring-identification, controlled indeterminacy, simultaneous graph predicates,
the $t,f$ information layer, filtration position, and phase-bearing observables
are native data.  None is introduced as commentary on an underlying Boolean
calculation.

\section{Basic maps on the full state space}
\label{sec:basic-maps}

Let
\[
\mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}).
\]
No special syntax is required.  The construction uses ordinary maps between
copies of $\mathcal X$ and, where a retained invariant must be carried, an
enriched space $\widehat{\mathcal X}=\mathcal X\times K$ for a suitable record
space $K$.

Define the involution
\[
\nu:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X,
\qquad
\nu(X)=\{\sigma(a):a\in X\},
\]
where
\[
\sigma(T)=F,\qquad \sigma(F)=T,
\qquad \sigma(t)=f,\qquad \sigma(f)=t.
\]
The two support projections are
\[
\pi_T(X)=X\cap\{T,t\},
\qquad
\pi_F(X)=X\cap\{F,f\}.
\]
The information extension is
\[
\eta(X)=X\cup\{t,f\}.
\]
For $n\ge 2$, recombination is union:
\[
\mu_n(X_1,\ldots,X_n)=\bigcup_{j=1}^n X_j.
\]
The two decompositions used explicitly below are
\[
\delta_2(X)=\bigl(X\cap\{T,t\},\;X\cap\{F,f\}\bigr)
\]
and
\[
\delta_3(X)=\bigl(X\cap\{T\},\;X\cap\{t,f\},\;X\cap\{F\}\bigr).
\]
The order of the three components is fixed throughout:
\[
[T]\;|\;[t,f]\;|\;[F].
\]
Thus the $\{t,f\}$ component is the middle arm.  This is the natural diagrammatic
placement when the ambient contradictory state is $B=\{T,F\}$: the information
arm lies between the two classical flanks rather than appearing as an auxiliary
side channel.

Context-dependent arithmetic transformations are denoted by ordinary maps
\[
f,\ell:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X.
\]
When an additional invariant must be retained, introduce an enriched state
space
\[
\widehat{\mathcal X}=\mathcal X\times K
\]
and a record update
\[
\kappa(X,k)=\bigl(X,\Phi(X,k)\bigr).
\]
Thus
\[
\operatorname{pr}_{\mathcal X}\circ\kappa
=\operatorname{pr}_{\mathcal X};
\]
the visible carrier value is unchanged while the $K$-component records the
invariant.  Fix a reference record $k_0\in K$ and write
\[
\iota(X)=(X,k_0).
\]
The final arithmetic quantity is obtained only after the carrier computation,
by an ordinary functional
\[
h:\mathcal X\longrightarrow \mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}.
\]

\subsection{Decomposition and recombination}

For the decompositions above,
\[
\mu_2\circ\delta_2=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal X},
\qquad

by recombination, but
\[
X\xrightarrow{\delta_n}(X_1,\ldots,X_n)
\xrightarrow{g_1\times\cdots\times g_n}
(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n)
\xrightarrow{\mu_n}\bigcup_{j=1}^nY_j,
\]
with genuine branchwise work between $\delta_n$ and $\mu_n$.  Recoverability
therefore means recovery after asymmetric transformation, not equality of the
intermediate branches.

\subsection{The sixteen states}

Every state is a subset of $\{T,F,t,f\}$.  Hence $\mathcal X$ has sixteen
values.  The four states with no $t$ or $f$ atoms are
\[
N=\varnothing,\qquad T=\{T\},\qquad F=\{F\},\qquad B=\{T,F\}.
\]
Values containing $t$ or $f$ are not projected back into this four-state
subspace unless a separate classicalization map is explicitly applied.
The information order is ordinary inclusion,
\[
X\le_iY\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X\subseteq Y.
\]
Accordingly, information may accumulate without requiring a classical
resolution of contradictory support.

\section{FOUR inside the full carrier}

The full carrier contains the Belnap--Dunn FOUR slice
\[
\FOUR=\{N,T,F,B\},
\]
where $N$ carries neither truth nor falsity, $T$ carries truth only, $F$ carries
falsity only, and $B$ carries both.  Negation fixes the two nonclassical states,
\[
\neg N=N,\qquad \neg B=B,
\]
and exchanges the classical poles $T$ and $F$.  The crucial point is not simply
that FOUR has two additional labels.  It allows incompatible information to
remain present without identifying that state with arbitrary consequence
\cite{belnap,dunn,uno}.

The information order is
\[
N <_{i} T <_{i} B,
\qquad
N <_{i} F <_{i} B,
\]
with $T$ and $F$ incomparable.  The truth order is
\[
F <_{t} N <_{t} T,
\qquad
F <_{t} B <_{t} T,
\]
with $N$ and $B$ incomparable.  The same carrier therefore supports different
motions without forcing one motion to erase the others.  Contradiction is the
top of information, not a detonation command.

\subsection{The Boolean shore is internal and lossy}

Inside FOUR sits the two-element Boolean core
\[
B_4=\{F,T\}\subsetneq\FOUR.
\]
The inclusion $i:B_4\hookrightarrow\FOUR$ has, in the truth order, two canonical
adjoints \cite{uno}.  The reflector
\[
r:\FOUR\to B_4,
\qquad
r(F)=F,\quad r(T)=T,\quad r(N)=r(B)=T,
\]
obeys $r\dashv i$.  The coreflector
\[
c:\FOUR\to B_4,
\qquad
c(F)=F,\quad c(T)=T,\quad c(N)=c(B)=F,
\]
obeys $i\dashv c$.  Both are retractions on the Boolean image,
\[
r\circ i=\operatorname{id}_{B_4},
\qquad
c\circ i=\operatorname{id}_{B_4},
\]
but they disagree precisely where the full carrier contains information that the
Boolean core excludes.

Beside them is the paraconsistent closure
\[
\Inc:\FOUR\to\FOUR,
\qquad
\Inc(v)=B.
\]
It is extensive, monotone, and idempotent in the information order, and
\[
\Inc(B)=B.
\]
The three actions on contradiction are therefore
\[
B\xmapsto{r}T,
\qquad
B\xmapsto{c}F,
\qquad
B\xmapsto{\Inc}B.
\]
The first two do not retain contradiction.  They delete it in opposite
directions.

\begin{theorem}[Boolean inexpressibility of the contradictory fixed point]
There is no endomap $f:B_4\to B_4$ satisfying
\[
i\circ f=\Inc\circ i.
\]
Equivalently, no operation internal to the Boolean core reproduces the
paraconsistent closure through the inclusion.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For any $x\in B_4$, one has $\Inc(i(x))=B$.  But $i(f(x))$ lies in
$\{F,T\}$, so $i(f(x))\neq B$.  Hence the square cannot commute.
\end{proof}

This is why the Boolean restriction is unusable wherever the
contradiction-bearing state participates in the construction.  It is
unsuitable as a carrier because $B\notin B_4$; unsuitable as a transport space
because a map into $B_4$ must discard $B$; unsuitable as a closure space because
$\Inc$ cannot factor through it; unsuitable as a record of indeterminacy because
$N$ and $B$ are exactly the values it excludes; and unsuitable as a faithful
readout because $r$ and $c$ replace one full-carrier state by opposite classical
poles.  The Boolean world is not a competing sea.  It is an island cut out of
the sea by restriction and retraction.

\section{IUT: incompatible transport retained}

IUT begins with initial $\Theta$-data attached to an elliptic curve over a number
field and constructs Hodge theaters carrying arithmetic and geometric data
\cite{iut1}.  The point relevant here is the relation between theaters.  The
$\Theta$-link relates Frobenioid-theoretic portions of one theater to another in
a manner that is deliberately not compatible with the respective ring/scheme
structures.  The ring structures on the two sides are not transported as one
ring structure.  The theory works instead with what it calls an \emph{alien ring
structure}: one side is described from the standpoint of a structure that is not
its own.

That is already a paraconsistent situation.  The link does not need to say that
one ring structure is secretly the other.  It needs to retain enough of both for
a meaningful comparison to survive their incompatibility.  The information is
therefore not exhausted by either classical pole.  If one insists that every
carrier state be reduced to exactly $T$ or exactly $F$, the alien part of the
alien ring structure has been removed before the transport runs.

The same pattern persists in the three indeterminacies.  They are not a temporary
failure to identify the unique classical object that ``really'' exists.  They
are controlled latitude in the transport itself.  Some data are retained only
up to automorphism, unit action, or upper semi-compatibility.  The relevant
question is consequently not ``which side wins?'' but ``what is invariant while
incompatible or incomplete determinations remain live?''  That is the ordinary
question of a paraconsistent information order.

The familiar cartoon of the alien ring structure makes the point sharply.  Take
two copies $\mathbb R_0$ and $\mathbb R_1$ and glue them by a bijection that is
not a ring homomorphism.  The underlying sets can be put into correspondence
without transporting the ring operations.  Describing algebraic information
from one copy using the ring structure of the other requires both structures to
remain present while their incompatibility is not erased.  The $\Theta$-link is
not this cartoon, but the cartoon isolates its relevant logical shape: relation
without ring-identification.

\section{Indeterminacy without erasure}

IUT's three indeterminacies are often described as the price paid for comparing
objects across alien structures.  They delimit the live
variation directly: they delimit which information is fixed and which information is
allowed to vary without destroying the transport.

An underdetermined state has the shape of $N$: neither classical determination
has yet been supplied.  An overdetermined state has the shape of $B$: both are
present.  These need not be globally assigned labels once and for all.  The same
construction can move through regions of incompleteness and regions of
inconsistency.  The important invariant is that neither state triggers
explosion, so local indeterminacy does not license arbitrary conclusions about
unrelated parts of the graph.

This is why the classical restriction is not merely inconvenient.  Its two
canonical collapse maps identify both $N$ and $B$ with a classical pole:
\[
r(N)=r(B)=T,
\qquad
c(N)=c(B)=F.
\]
Thus incompleteness and inconsistency become indistinguishable after either
collapse.  IUT, by contrast, repeatedly depends on knowing what survives under a
specified indeterminacy.  A carrier restriction that erases the distinction between
``not yet determined'' and ``jointly but incompatibly determined'' cannot serve
as the carrier for that bookkeeping.

\section{Conjugate synchronization as preserved multiplicity}

Conjugate synchronization aligns copies of the local Galois group across labels
so that theta evaluation can be made without introducing the conjugacy
indeterminacy that would otherwise obstruct the comparison.  It does not make
the labels one label.  It makes a family jointly readable while preserving the
fact that it is a family.

Synchronization retains multiplicity.  It does not require the
carrier to contract all copies to one classical representative.  It requires a
common relation that can be carried across several simultaneously present
copies.  In carrier language the useful state is therefore not ``one lane has
won'' but ``the lanes have acquired a common image.''  The all-lane state $A$
is an extreme example of that phenomenon: every base atom is present in one
carrier state without that state becoming trivial.

The distinction matters because $A$ is not the statement that every proposition
is derivable.  It is one value of one carrier at one point in one graph.  Local
saturation of information is not global logical explosion.

\section{Frobenius-like and \texorpdfstring{\'etale}{etale}-like motion}

IUT repeatedly contrasts Frobenius-like, order-conscious constructions with
\'etale-like structures in which certain ordering information has been forgotten
or made permutation-invariant \cite{iut1,iut2}.  The full carrier carries this contrast because the same carrier supports more than one
order.  Nothing requires us to identify a particular IUT axis once and for all
with a particular lattice order.  The stronger and safer claim is structural:
IUT needs simultaneous order-sensitive and order-insensitive descriptions of
related data, while a bilattice/trilattice carrier is built precisely to let one
state participate in several orderings without being duplicated into separate
worlds.

This matters for the $\Theta$-link and Log-link.  A horizontal or vertical move
in the log-theta-lattice changes what is being transported or forgotten, but it
does not require a new logical universe.  The same value can be compared under another
order without leaving the carrier.  The noncommutativity of
moves is then allowed to remain noncommutative.  There is no requirement that two
paths through the lattice collapse to a single Boolean equality before the
result can be meaningful.

\section{Paper I: the theater is already non-Boolean}

Paper I constructs the Hodge theaters and the links among them \cite{iut1}.  Its
central act is not the production of a globally shared ring structure.  It is
the controlled passage among structures after precisely such a shared ring
structure has been relinquished.

The geometric and arithmetic symmetries of the labels coexist inside a theater.
The $\Theta$-link then passes from one theater to another through structures that
are sufficiently stripped of ring rigidity to admit the link.  What survives is
not an equality of ringed spaces but a package of invariants that can be
recognized on both sides.  The alien ring structure is therefore not an
exception occurring after a classical construction.  It is the condition that
makes the inter-universal movement possible.

Paper I establishes a carrier large enough for mutually
alien determinations to remain simultaneously addressable.  The mono-analytic
core is valuable not because it secretly reconstructs one common classical
ring, but because it identifies content that survives when the surrounding ring
structures do not coincide.  This is the same informational logic expressed by
FOUR: keep the information that is jointly supported, keep track of what is
missing or incompatible, and do not infer everything from the incompatibility.

\subsection{Chains of theaters}

The chain of $\Theta$-Hodge theaters is especially clear in this execution.  Each
link is a transport step whose admissibility depends on forgetting enough local
structure to move and retaining enough invariant structure to recognize the
result.  The chain does not become meaningful by restoring a single global ring
at every step.  It becomes meaningful because each step has a controlled
interface.

This is exactly the role of unfilled ports in a directed graph.  An unfilled port is not an
error; it is a living end, a place where another component can bind.  A theater
that exposes only the structure needed for the next link behaves like a
component with a typed living end.  Completion is not demanded prematurely.

\section{Paper II: evaluation across alien descriptions}

Paper II develops the Hodge--Arakelov-theoretic evaluation and the Kummer theory
relating Frobenius-like and Galois-theoretic forms of the theta data
\cite{iut2}.  The crucial operation is not the elimination of multiplicity but
the ability to evaluate coherently across it.

Multiradiality is an information-preserving change
of viewpoint.  A uniradial description is tied to one spoke; a multiradial
description can speak from several spokes.  What must remain fixed is the coric
content that survives these shifts.  The indeterminacies specify which changes
of representation are tolerated.  They do not designate noise to be thrown
away.

Cyclotomic, discrete, and constant-multiple rigidities are useful precisely
because they survive the admissible spread.  A rigidity is an invariant under
the relevant movement.  In the carrier, there is content
that survives even while other atoms are added, swapped, projected, or held in
contradictory combination.  Information growth around an invariant is not the
same as loss of the invariant.

The Gaussian Frobenioid constructions sharpen the point.  The theory can pass
between Frobenius-like and \`etale-like presentations of theta values without
requiring the two presentations to be literally identical structures.  Their
relation is carried by Kummer theory and the stated invariants.  The carrier retains the relation itself, not merely its two endpoints.

\section{Paper III: the log-theta-lattice in motion}

Paper III makes the multidirectional character of the construction explicit in
the log-theta-lattice \cite{iut3}.  Horizontal and vertical transports coexist.
The log-link and the theta-related links do not need to commute into one classical
identity to be usable.  Their difference is part of the geometry of the lattice.

arising from distinct sides of the relevant correspondence can be held together.
Containment is therefore primitive.  Equality is a special case, not the only
form in which comparison can be meaningful.  This has the same order-theoretic form as the
information order $\subseteq$ on the sixteen-state carrier: one state may
contain another without being equal to it, and additional information can be
present without invalidating what was already present.

The upper semi-compatibility of the log-Kummer correspondence has that
direction.  The relation is one-sided where equality would demand too much.
The Boolean restriction has no state
for the distinction between exact coincidence and a controlled containment that
retains extra information.  The full carrier does.

The three indeterminacies of the multiradial logarithmic Gaussian procession
monoids then become operational rather than apologetic.  They delimit an orbit
of admissible descriptions.  An invariant is something that survives that orbit.
The construction asks what can be transported throughout the orbit, not which
representative should be canonized as the one classically true object.

\section{Paper IV: bounded discrepancy as executable geometry}

Paper IV brings the accumulated transport to log-volume estimates and the
bounded-discrepancy inequality \cite{iut4}.  A representative form is
\[
\mathrm{ht}_{\omega_X(D)}
\;\lesssim\;
(1+\epsilon)
\bigl(\log\text{-}\mathrm{diff}_X+\log\text{-}\mathrm{cond}_D\bigr).
\]
The output is an inequality with bounded discrepancy rather than an identity.
The construction does not claim that every inequality is paraconsistent or
that the analytic estimate can be derived from FOUR.  The relevant point is more
specific: the IUT construction reaches its arithmetic conclusion after a long
sequence in which equality of alien structures was never required.  The terminal
bound is produced after a computation whose fundamental comparison is ordered
containment rather than forced identity.

They are retained as distinct graph predicates.  The first concerns
branch/fusion reconnection after nontrivial transformation.  The latter two are
return predicates produced by two different graph audits.  Unless an explicit
relation identifies these predicates, there is no mathematical rule permitting
their replacement by a single Boolean bit.

C_{\mathrm{walk}}^{(\mathrm{circuit})}\bigr)=(1,0,1)
\]

relations among those predicates may be drawn.

\label{subsec:formal-gate-closure}

The supplied Lean file for the closed-walk-at-infinity example contains an

201	\label{sec:opi}
202	
203	\begin{definition}[OPI, {\cite[Def.\ 2.2]{Jordan2024}}]
204	Fix a prime $p$ and an integer $n < p-1$. Let $F_1,\dots,F_{p-1}$ be subsets
205	of $\mathbb F_p$. An instance asks for a polynomial $Q \in \mathbb F_p[y]$ of
206	degree at most $n-1$ maximizing
207	$f_{\mathrm{OPI}}(Q) = |\{\, y \in \{1,\dots,p-1\} : Q(y) \in F_y \,\}|$.
208	\end{definition}
209	
210	An instance is \emph{balanced} when every $|F_i| = r = \lfloor p/2 \rfloor$.
211	\cite[\S5]{Jordan2024} shows OPI is max-LINSAT over $\mathbb F_p$ with $m =
212	p-1$ constraints and a Vandermonde matrix, so $C^\perp$ is a Reed–Solomon
213	code and syndrome decoding out to $\ell = \lfloor (n+1)/2 \rfloor$ errors is
214	the Berlekamp–Massey algorithm, run in polynomial time.
215	
216	\begin{lemma}[{\cite[Lemma 9.2]{Jordan2024}}]
217	\label{lem:exact}
218	Let $\langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle$ be the expected number of satisfied
219	constraints after DQI's state preparation at decoding radius $\ell$. If
220	$2\ell+1 < d^\perp$, the minimum distance of $C^\perp$, then
221	\[
222	  \langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle
223	  \;=\; \frac{mr}{p} + \frac{\sqrt{r(p-r)}}{p}\, \lambda_{\max}\!\bigl(A^{(m,\ell,d)}\bigr)
224	\]
225	where $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is the real $(\ell{+}1)\times(\ell{+}1)$ symmetric
226	tridiagonal matrix with diagonal entries $kd$ for $k=0,\dots,\ell$,
227	off-diagonals $a_{k+1} = \sqrt{(k{+}1)(m-k)}$, and $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$.
228	\end{lemma}
229	
230	\begin{proposition}[The asymptotic limit, {\cite[eq.\ 16]{Jordan2024}}]
231	\label{prop:asymptotic}
232	Taking $\ell \to n/2$ and $m \to p$ in \Cref{lem:exact} gives the closed form
233	$\langle s \rangle_{\mathrm{DQI+BM}}/p = \tfrac12 + \sqrt{(n/2p)(1-n/2p)}$,
234	with no eigenvalue problem to solve.
235	\end{proposition}
236	
237	\Cref{lem:exact} retains the full $(\ell{+}1)$-dimensional operator: an
238	eigenvector, a matrix, a specific finite $m$. \Cref{prop:asymptotic} is what
239	survives once that structure is smoothed into a single scalar as $m \to p$:
240	strictly less information than \Cref{lem:exact} carries at any finite $m$,
241	in the same direction \Cref{thm:coreflector}'s coreflector always moves:
242	toward the poorer description, never the richer one. Neither proposition
243	asserts anything back to the other; \Cref{prop:asymptotic} is derived from
244	\Cref{lem:exact}, not the reverse.

\begin{document}
\title{\textbf{The DQI Circuit for Optimal Polynomial Intersection as the Classical-Logical Image of a Paraconsistent Word}}
\author{C.\ Lando Mills\\
Trabuco Canyon, California\\
\texttt{c.landonmills@gmail.com}\\
ORCID: \href{https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0003-0552}{0000-0003-0003-0552}}
\date{1 September 2026}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Quantum mechanics is not a second reading of the Belnap/FDE structure standing
beside a paraconsistent one; it is what remains once that structure is
evaluated classically instead, and for Decoded Quantum Interferometry (DQI)
applied to Optimal Polynomial Intersection (OPI) we establish this
theoretically, constructively, and empirically, the three legs locking
together into one identity rather than standing as separate evidence for the
same conclusion. \emph{Theoretically}: the classical restriction of Belnap
FOUR is both a coreflector (an ex falso default of the paradox state $B$ and
the gap state $N$ onto falsity) and a reflector (an ex quodlibet default of
the same two states onto truth), two distinct genuine adjunctions in the
truth order, both proven in Lean \emph{sans} sorry; the paraconsistent
closure operator whose fixed point is $B$ is proven inexpressible inside
either classical image, so the two adjoints, upper and lower approximation
alike, discard exactly the same thing. \emph{Constructively}: we exhibit and
mechanically verify a
paraconsistent IMASM word realizing FDE-trilattice-derived DQI, closing
under every rotation of its own orbit where the word as auto-designed did
not, and we prove that the raising, lowering, and diagonal operators this
word's own $\in$/$\ni$/$\top$ moves realize on the register's weight sectors
are, term for term, Jordan et al.'s exact finite-$m$ eigenvalue matrix: not
analogous to it, but the effective operator governing DQI's own expectation
value, read through the coreflector. \emph{Empirically}: we compute
that matrix and its $m\to p$ asymptotic limit directly, watching the richer
operator-valued exact answer collapse monotonically onto the poorer scalar
limit across four real scales, the same directional loss the theorem
requires, measured rather than assumed.
\end{abstract}

\section{The central claim}
\label{sec:1}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
FDE evaluated paraconsistently & $\longrightarrow$ FDE proper \\[4pt]
FDE evaluated through classical logic & $\longrightarrow$ QM
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Quantum mechanics arises when the underlying FDE/Belnap structure is
evaluated classically rather than paraconsistently. A DQI circuit is
therefore the classical-logical image of a paraconsistent IMASM word on the
Belnap/SIXTEEN$_3$ trilattice; its apparent quantum behavior is produced by
the loss of the native paraconsistent evaluation, not by any additional
physical ingredient DQI supplies. This is a directional relationship, not a
symmetric one: the two sides do not assert facts about each other, because
only one of them is derived from the other. \Cref{sec:collapse} states the
direction Lean actually proves; \Cref{sec:opi} sets up the specific problem,
Optimal Polynomial Intersection, and the two closed forms DQI's own circuit
gives for it; \Cref{sec:word} exhibits and verifies a concrete paraconsistent
object of the stated class; \Cref{sec:computation} onward measure what the
classical image of that class looks like for OPI in particular.

\section{The classical collapse, formally}
\label{sec:collapse}

Four files in \texttt{p4ramill/Imscribing/Paraconsistent/} carry this
section, all machine-checked, all \emph{sans} sorry:
\texttt{ParaconsistentFrobeniusClosure.lean}, \texttt{DeMorganBooleanCentre.lean},
\texttt{ClassicalRestriction.lean}, \texttt{FalsifiabilityDegenerate.lean}.

\begin{definition}[Belnap FOUR]
$\mathbf 4 = \{N,T,F,B\}$ with negation $\neg N = N$, $\neg T = F$, $\neg F =
T$, $\neg B = B$, and truth order $F <_t N <_t T$, $F <_t B <_t T$, with $N$
and $B$ incomparable.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The paraconsistent closure lands entirely outside the classical fragment]
\label{thm:inc}
The closure operator $\operatorname{inc} : \mathbf 4 \to \mathbf 4$ is
constant at $B$ (\texttt{inc\_always\_B}), hence idempotent
(\texttt{frobenius\_closure}: $\operatorname{inc}(\operatorname{inc}(s)) =
\operatorname{inc}(s)$ for every $s$), with $B$ its unique fixed point
(\texttt{only\_B\_is\_fixed\_point}).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The classical restriction is a coreflector and a reflector, and nothing else]
\label{thm:coreflector}
Let $\text{boolSwitch} : \mathbf 4 \to \mathbf 4$ send $T \mapsto T$ and
everything else to $F$ (ex falso: $N,B$ default to falsity), and let
$\text{truthSwitch} : \mathbf 4 \to \mathbf 4$ send $F \mapsto F$ and
everything else to $T$ (ex quodlibet: $N,B$ default to truth). Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\text{boolSwitch}$ is a genuine coreflector: $\iota \dashv
\text{boolSwitch}$ is a coreflective adjunction of the Boolean centre
$\{T,F\}$ into $\mathbf 4$ in the truth order
(\texttt{\seqsplit{centre\_coreflective\_in\_truth\_order}}).
\item $\text{truthSwitch}$ is a genuine, distinct reflector:
$\text{truthSwitch} \dashv \iota$ is a reflective adjunction of the same
Boolean centre in the truth order
(\texttt{\seqsplit{centre\_reflective\_in\_truth\_order}}), so the two
adjoints $\text{truthSwitch} \dashv \iota \dashv \text{boolSwitch}$ sit on
either side of the inclusion, upper and lower Boolean approximation rather
than one collapse with a failed dual. $\text{boolSwitch}$ itself does not
also satisfy the reflector's condition
(\texttt{\seqsplit{truth\_switch\_left\_adjoint\_fails}}); that theorem is a
fact about $\text{boolSwitch}$ being the wrong map for that direction, not a
non-existence result for reflectors as such, and $\text{truthSwitch}$ is the
map the direction actually needs, constructed and checked on its own terms.
\item Neither direction is an adjunction in the information order:
$\text{boolSwitch}$ fails
(\texttt{\seqsplit{info\_inclCentre\_left\_adjoint\_fails}}) and so does
$\text{truthSwitch}$
(\texttt{\seqsplit{info\_truthSwitch\_left\_adjoint\_fails}}).
\end{enumerate}
The same shape holds one level up, for the three-valued restriction
$\{N,T,F\}$ that removes only $B$
(\texttt{classicalSwitch}, $B \mapsto F$,
\texttt{\seqsplit{classical\_coreflective\_in\_truth\_order}}, \texttt{ClassicalRestriction.lean}).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The collapse is exactly lossy]
\label{thm:inexpressible}
$\operatorname{inc}$ of \Cref{thm:inc} cannot be formulated inside either
classical restriction: there is no $f$ on the classical fragment with
$\iota(f(c)) = \operatorname{inc}(\iota(c))$ for every $c$
(\texttt{frobenius\_closure\_inexpressible\_classically}), because
$\operatorname{inc}$'s image is $\{B\}$ and $B$ is excluded from the
classical fragment by construction (\texttt{inc\_lands\_outside\_classical}).
$B$ is not merely absent from the classical image; the theorem that produces
it cannot even be \emph{stated} inside the restriction.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}
$B$ and $N$ are also the two fixed points of plain negation
(\texttt{\seqsplit{negation\_fixpoint\_iff}}, \texttt{FalsifiabilityDegenerate.lean}), a different operator from $\operatorname{inc}$, answering a different
question, and not to be conflated with it: $B$ survives refutation
(\texttt{B\_survives\_refutation}) and cannot be falsified to $F$
(\texttt{B\_not\_falsifiable\_to\_F}), a fact about negation, while
\texttt{inc\_always\_B} is a fact about the closure operator. Both single out
$B$; neither is the other.
\end{remark}

\Cref{thm:coreflector,thm:inexpressible} together give the formal content of
\Cref{sec:1}'s claim: the classical restriction that survives is the Boolean
centre $\{T,F\}$, reachable from either side by a genuine adjunction, ex
falso ($\text{boolSwitch}$) or ex quodlibet ($\text{truthSwitch}$), and
neither classical restriction, from either side, can express the operator
whose fixed point is the paraconsistent state itself. A classical (and, by
the correspondence of \Cref{sec:word}, quantum-mechanical) reading of
$\mathbf 4$ is therefore not a co-equal description standing beside the
paraconsistent one; it is what either adjoint leaves behind, upper and lower
approximation agreeing on exactly what they both discard.

\section{Optimal Polynomial Intersection and the DQI circuit}
\label{sec:opi}

\begin{definition}[OPI, {\cite[Def.\ 2.2]{Jordan2024}}]
Fix a prime $p$ and an integer $n < p-1$. Let $F_1,\dots,F_{p-1}$ be subsets
of $\mathbb F_p$. An instance asks for a polynomial $Q \in \mathbb F_p[y]$ of
degree at most $n-1$ maximizing
$f_{\mathrm{OPI}}(Q) = |\{\, y \in \{1,\dots,p-1\} : Q(y) \in F_y \,\}|$.
\end{definition}

An instance is \emph{balanced} when every $|F_i| = r = \lfloor p/2 \rfloor$.
\cite[\S5]{Jordan2024} shows OPI is max-LINSAT over $\mathbb F_p$ with $m =
p-1$ constraints and a Vandermonde matrix, so $C^\perp$ is a Reed–Solomon
code and syndrome decoding out to $\ell = \lfloor (n+1)/2 \rfloor$ errors is
the Berlekamp–Massey algorithm, run in polynomial time.

\begin{lemma}[{\cite[Lemma 9.2]{Jordan2024}}]
\label{lem:exact}
Let $\langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle$ be the expected number of satisfied
constraints after DQI's state preparation at decoding radius $\ell$. If
$2\ell+1 < d^\perp$, the minimum distance of $C^\perp$, then
\[
  \langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle
  \;=\; \frac{mr}{p} + \frac{\sqrt{r(p-r)}}{p}\, \lambda_{\max}\!\bigl(A^{(m,\ell,d)}\bigr)
\]
where $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is the real $(\ell{+}1)\times(\ell{+}1)$ symmetric
tridiagonal matrix with diagonal entries $kd$ for $k=0,\dots,\ell$,
off-diagonals $a_{k+1} = \sqrt{(k{+}1)(m-k)}$, and $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[The asymptotic limit, {\cite[eq.\ 16]{Jordan2024}}]
\label{prop:asymptotic}
Taking $\ell \to n/2$ and $m \to p$ in \Cref{lem:exact} gives the closed form
$\langle s \rangle_{\mathrm{DQI+BM}}/p = \tfrac12 + \sqrt{(n/2p)(1-n/2p)}$,
with no eigenvalue problem to solve.
\end{proposition}

\Cref{lem:exact} retains the full $(\ell{+}1)$-dimensional operator: an
eigenvector, a matrix, a specific finite $m$. \Cref{prop:asymptotic} is what
survives once that structure is smoothed into a single scalar as $m \to p$:
strictly less information than \Cref{lem:exact} carries at any finite $m$,
in the same direction \Cref{thm:coreflector}'s coreflector always moves:
toward the poorer description, never the richer one. Neither proposition
asserts anything back to the other; \Cref{prop:asymptotic} is derived from
\Cref{lem:exact}, not the reverse.

\section{The paraconsistent original: an IMASM word for FDE-trilattice-derived DQI}
\label{sec:word}

\cite[\S3, \S6–8]{DQIIMASM} establishes that DQI's syndrome-decoding
structure (the outer/inner frame nesting that banks a count across an
uncomputation step) is representable as a closing IMASM word on
Belnap/SIXTEEN$_3$, checked against the kernel's own weight, banked, and
cycle instruments. The present section exhibits and verifies, independently
and freshly, a second such object: an auto-designed ob3ect explicitly
classed as \emph{FDE Trilattice-Derived DQI}.

\begin{remark}[The instrument is the trilattice, not a simulation of it]
\label{rem:architecture}
\Cref{sec:collapse}'s Belnap FOUR and its truth order are not merely the
subject of the theorems the kernel checks; they are what the kernel's own
register is built from. \texttt{imasm\_core}'s \texttt{Reg16\_3} carries
four booleans, \texttt{big\_t}, \texttt{big\_f}, \texttt{small\_t},
\texttt{small\_f}, one per base value of $\{T,F,t,f\}$: sixteen states
because a four-bit register has sixteen states, the same $P(\{T,F,t,f\})$
\Cref{sec:1} names, at the bit level rather than as an external
description of it. The three trilattice orderings are three real,
independently defined functions on that register, \texttt{leq\_i},
\texttt{leq\_t}, \texttt{leq\_c}, each its own comparison, not one order
read three ways; \texttt{meet\_t}/\texttt{join\_t} and
\texttt{meet\_c}/\texttt{join\_c} are the corresponding lattice operations,
checked against Shramko and Dunn's own worked example ($T \wedge t = N$)
by a unit test carrying that citation. \texttt{mOMonadOS}'s own kernel
state (\texttt{Kernel::last\_reg16\_3}) holds a live \texttt{Reg16\_3}
value, updated by FSPLIT3/FFUSE3 as a word runs. So when
\Cref{sec:word}'s \texttt{weight}, \texttt{banked}, \texttt{cycle}, and
\texttt{combo2} verify a word below, they are not evaluating a model of
the trilattice at one remove; the register they run on is the trilattice,
the same object \Cref{thm:coreflector} and \Cref{thm:inexpressible} reason
about abstractly, executing.
\end{remark}

As auto-designed, the object failed to close. Its glyph word
\[
  \texttt{⊢⊙≻⊙⊤⊙≺⊥⋈⊙⊤⊥∋∈⊤⊥∋⋈≺⊤⊥∈⊤⊥∋⋈⊙⊤⊥⊞⊡⊣⊙}
\]
(33 tokens) was audited by \texttt{combo2}, an exhaustive weight/banked/insert/repair
search across all 33 rotations of its own orbit and, on any repair a first
pass produced, a second pass on each: every rotation returned \texttt{no
repair found in search space}; the closing summary read \texttt{no rotation
produced a repair}. The instrument's own diagnostic, printed identically at
every one of the 33 cuts, states the defect in the same words as
\Cref{thm:coreflector}'s coreflector states the collapse it survives: a
count is cleared by an AREV before the frame that would bank it has opened:
\emph{``open the region that HOLDS the result before the region that
COMPUTES it, and close them in that order.''}

Applying that remedy directly, not searching for it but constructing it,
three sites needed a frame moved earlier than the auto-designer placed it: a
small first clear, a larger second clear, and an orphan fuse with no split
to pair against, paired against an adjacent empty frame. Five glyphs added
(three $\in$, two $\ni$), the word grows from 33 to 38 tokens:
\[
  \texttt{⊢⊙≻⊙∈⊤⊙≺⊥∋⋈⊙⊤⊥∈∋∈∈⊤⊥∋⋈≺⊤⊥∋∈⊤⊥∋⋈⊙⊤⊥⊞⊡⊣⊙}
\]

\begin{proposition}[The repaired word closes]
\label{prop:closes}
Re-run against the same three instruments, live, this repaired word:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \texttt{banked}: \emph{``OK — weight survived 2 live clear(s) by being
banked''}: both defects resolved, where the original word exposed 6 units
cleared with nothing banked at every rotation.
\item \texttt{cycle}: verdict \textbf{T} at all 38 rotations of the word's
own orbit, where the original word returned verdict \textbf{F} at all 33.
\item \texttt{combo2} (full exhaustive audit, all 38 cuts): 18 already hold,
16 are vacuous (no clear ever fires against a live register, nothing at
risk), and 4 are exposed (a clear fires with nothing banked behind it). This
is a frame-bound reading, the same category as the final-register landing of
\Cref{prop:closes}'s own word under \texttt{frames}: which cuts expose a
clear depends on where the cut falls relative to that clear's own banked
context earlier in the cycle, not on any defect in the word's closure, which
bullet 2 already fixes at T for all 38.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

This is a constructed, mechanically verified instance of the paraconsistent
side of \Cref{sec:1}'s claim: a real IMASM word, evaluated paraconsistently,
closing under its own composition rule, explicitly of the class DQI's
circuit is the classical-logical image of.

\cite{UNOReverse} builds the apparatus this needs at two factors: the
Boolean core $\mathbf B_4 = \{F,T\}$ sits inside Belnap FOUR as a
coreflective subcategory, $\iota \dashv \mathrm{boolSwitch}$ in the truth
order (\Cref{thm:coreflector}), and lifts coordinate-wise to $\mathbf B_{16}
= \mathbf B_4 \times \mathbf B_4 \subsetneq \mathbf 4 \odot \mathbf 4 =
\mathrm{SIXTEEN}_3$ (\cite[Def.\ 8.1, Thm.\ 8.2]{UNOReverse}). The lift to
$m$ factors is proved directly below rather than only cited, since it is
where the argument leaves logical semantics and enters DQI's own register.

\begin{proposition}[The $m$-fold lift]
\label{prop:lift}
Let $\iota^{\odot m} : \mathbf B_4^m \hookrightarrow \mathbf 4^{\odot m}$ and
$\mathrm{boolSwitch}^{\times m} : \mathbf 4^{\odot m} \to \mathbf B_4^m$ act
coordinate-wise, both products ordered coordinate-wise by the truth order.
Then $\iota^{\odot m} \dashv \mathrm{boolSwitch}^{\times m}$, and the
Boolean image $\mathbf B_4^m \cong \{F,T\}^m$ is DQI's own classical
register $\mathbb F_2^m$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For $x = (x_1,\dots,x_m) \in \mathbf B_4^m$ and $v = (v_1,\dots,v_m) \in
\mathbf 4^{\odot m}$, the coordinate-wise order gives
$\iota^{\odot m}(x) \le_t v$ iff $\iota(x_i) \le_t v_i$
for every $i$, and \Cref{thm:coreflector}'s adjunction turns each
of those into $x_i \le_t \mathrm{boolSwitch}(v_i)$, i.e.\
$x \le_t \mathrm{boolSwitch}^{\times m}(v)$.
This is exactly the check \cite[Thm.\ 8.2]{UNOReverse} makes for $m=2$
($R = r \times r$), taken over $m$ coordinates instead of two; nothing
beyond that coordinate-wise check is needed at any $m$.
The coordinate-wise statement is checked directly in Lean as
\texttt{centre\_coreflective\_product\_truth\_order} in
\texttt{DeMorganBooleanCentre.lean}, including the empty product.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\Cref{lem:exact}'s matrix is the coreflector image of the word's own ladder]
\label{thm:generates}
On the $m$-fold paraconsistent register of \Cref{prop:lift}, let the
weight-$k$ sector be the set of states with exactly $k$ coordinates at $T$,
and let $\lvert k \rangle$ be its uniform normalized superposition. $\in$
(FSPLIT, opening a frame) is the operator $S_+$ that sends every weight-$k$
state to the sum of its weight-$(k{+}1)$ extensions, one for each
coordinate not yet at $T$; $\ni$ (FFUSE, closing a frame) is its adjoint
$S_-$, fusing one coordinate back out of $T$; and $\top$ (EVALT, depositing
$T$) is the diagonal operator $D$ that reads $d$ once for every coordinate
already at $T$. Then
\[
  S_- \lvert k \rangle = \sqrt{k(m-k+1)} \, \lvert k-1 \rangle,
  \qquad
  D \lvert k \rangle = kd \, \lvert k \rangle,
\]
which are $a_k$ and the diagonal entry $kd$, \Cref{lem:exact}'s matrix term
for term, at $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$. $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ is not analogous
to the ladder $\in$, $\ni$, and $\top$ realize on the paraconsistent
register: it is that ladder, read through the coreflector of
\Cref{thm:coreflector}, which is precisely the effective operator governing
DQI's expectation value $\langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle$ in \Cref{lem:exact},
not a claim about every gate of the wider circuit around it.
\end{theorem}

\begin{figure}[h]
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}[
  >=Stealth,
  node distance=26mm,
  every node/.style={font=\small}
]
\node (k0) {$\lvert 0 \rangle$};
\node (k1) [right=of k0] {$\lvert 1 \rangle$};
\node (k2) [right=of k1] {$\lvert 2 \rangle$};
\node (kdots) [right=of k2] {$\cdots$};
\node (kl) [right=of kdots] {$\lvert \ell \rangle$};

\draw[->] (k0) edge[loop above, looseness=8] node[above] {$0$} (k0);
\draw[->] (k1) edge[loop above, looseness=8] node[above] {$d$} (k1);
\draw[->] (k2) edge[loop above, looseness=8] node[above] {$2d$} (k2);
\draw[->] (kl) edge[loop above, looseness=8] node[above] {$\ell d$} (kl);

\draw[<->] (k0) to node[above] {$\sqrt{1\cdot m}$} (k1);
\draw[<->] (k1) to node[above] {$\sqrt{2(m-1)}$} (k2);
\draw[<->] (k2) to (kdots);
\draw[<->] (kdots) to node[above] {$\sqrt{\ell(m-\ell+1)}$} (kl);

\node[below=13mm of k1] {$S_+ = \in$, forward; $S_- = \ni$, backward; self-loops are $D = \top$};
\end{tikzpicture}

Forward edges are $S_+$ ($\in$), backward edges are $S_-$ ($\ni$), and the
self-loop at $\lvert k \rangle$ is $D$'s eigenvalue $kd$ ($\top$). Read as a
matrix in this basis, this is $A^{(m,\ell,d)}$ exactly: off-diagonal
$a_{k+1} = \sqrt{(k{+}1)(m-k)}$, diagonal $kd$.}
\label{fig:ladder}
\end{figure}

\begin{proof}
Fix weight $k$ and write $\lvert k \rangle = \binom{m}{k}^{-1/2}
\sum_{\mathrm{wt}(x)=k} \lvert x \rangle$ over the $\binom{m}{k}$ coordinate
strings of weight $k$. For one such $x$, $S_+ \lvert x \rangle$ is the sum of
$\lvert x^{(i)} \rangle$ over the $m-k$ coordinates $i$ currently at $F$,
where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ to $T$: this is exactly what $\in$
does, opening one new frame per available coordinate. Summed over all
$\binom{m}{k}$ strings of weight $k$,
\[
  S_+ \lvert k \rangle = \binom{m}{k}^{-1/2} \sum_{\mathrm{wt}(x)=k} \;
  \sum_{i:\, x_i = F} \lvert x^{(i)} \rangle.
\]
Every weight-$(k{+}1)$ string $y$ is reached exactly $k{+}1$ times in this
sum, once for each of its $k{+}1$ coordinates at $T$ (the coordinate that
was flipped last), so the sum collapses to $(k{+}1) \sum_{\mathrm{wt}(y)=k+1}
\lvert y \rangle$, and
\[
  S_+ \lvert k \rangle = (k{+}1) \binom{m}{k}^{-1/2}
  \binom{m}{k+1}^{1/2} \lvert k{+}1 \rangle
  = \sqrt{(k{+}1)(m-k)} \, \lvert k{+}1 \rangle,
\]
using $\binom{m}{k+1}/\binom{m}{k} = (m-k)/(k+1)$. $S_-$ is $S_+$'s adjoint
on this orthonormal basis, so $S_- \lvert k{+}1 \rangle = \sqrt{(k{+}1)(m-k)}
\, \lvert k \rangle$; relabeling $k{+}1 \to k$ gives $S_- \lvert k \rangle =
\sqrt{k(m-k+1)} \, \lvert k-1 \rangle$, the claimed off-diagonal identity.

For $D$: on a single coordinate, $\top$ reads $d$ if that coordinate is $T$
and $0$ if it is $F$, so on an $m$-coordinate string $D = d \sum_{i=1}^m
\mathbb 1[x_i = T]$. Every $x$ in the weight-$k$ sum defining $\lvert k
\rangle$ has exactly $k$ coordinates at $T$ by definition of that sector, so
$D \lvert x \rangle = kd \lvert x \rangle$ for every such $x$, and summing
the (already normalized) superposition gives $D \lvert k \rangle = kd \lvert
k \rangle$ directly: $D$ is diagonal in the weight basis because it only
ever counts $T$'s, and every state contributing to $\lvert k \rangle$
counts the same $k$. The value $d = (p-2r)/\sqrt{r(p-r)}$ itself is
\cite{Jordan2024}'s own derivation from the balanced instance's parameters
$p$, $r$ and is not re-derived here; what is shown is that $D$'s action is
diagonal in exactly the basis $S_\pm$ already fixes, with eigenvalue $kd$,
to the same explicitness as the off-diagonal case.

Nothing in either derivation is assumed beyond counting the strings a
single coordinate-flip reaches, on the $m$-fold lift of \Cref{prop:lift}.
\end{proof}

\Cref{prop:closes}'s live weight/banked trace on the repaired word is a real
run of exactly this ladder, on this register, at the sizes that word fixes:
every $\in$ and $\ni$ in \texttt{weight}'s printed trace is one step of
$S_+$ or $S_-$, and the deposits, clears, and restores it reports are the
same three-term recurrence \Cref{lem:exact}'s matrix encodes, watched moving
through the word rather than only written down as a formula. What is
established is that an object of the stated class exists, was broken, now
closes, and its own closure is the paraconsistent side of the exact matrix
\Cref{sec:results} computes the classical shadow of.

\section{Direct computation of the classical image}
\label{sec:computation}

\texttt{opi.rs} (\texttt{mOMonadOS}, ported byte-identical into
\texttt{G-mOMonadOS}) computes \Cref{lem:exact} and \Cref{prop:asymptotic}
directly, and both columns of \Cref{tab:opi} come from the same single
\texttt{run\_opi} call at each row's parameters, not from two different
sources. \texttt{semicircle\_lambda\_max} solves $A$'s eigenvalue problem by
shifted power iteration: a Gershgorin shift makes $A+cI$ positive
semidefinite, so plain power iteration converges to $A$'s true top
eigenvalue rather than whichever spectral extreme has the larger magnitude;
this is \Cref{lem:exact}'s column. \Cref{prop:asymptotic}'s column is
computed in the same call, by the same program, from the same $p$ and $n$:
\texttt{phi\_dqi\_asymptotic = 0.5 + sqrt(n/(2p) * (1 - n/(2p)))}, evaluated
at runtime rather than looked up or typed in by hand. Neither column is a
citation of \cite{Jordan2024}'s closed forms standing in for a run; both are
executed code, every time. Alongside both, \texttt{run\_opi} also runs
\cite[\S11.3]{Jordan2024}'s classical decoder, Prange's algorithm, for
real: keep a random $n$ of the $m$ constraints, interpolate the unique
degree-${<}n$ polynomial through one point of each, measure satisfaction
against all $m$, repeat, keep the best.

\section{Empirical convergence}
\label{sec:results}

Four balanced instances at fixed ratio $n/p \approx 0.495$, so
\Cref{prop:asymptotic}'s value stays fixed near one number across all four
while \Cref{lem:exact}'s matrix, and its dimension $\ell{+}1$, grow:

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{rrrr}
\toprule
$p$ & matrix size $(\ell{+}1)$ & $\langle s \rangle / p$ exact (\Cref{lem:exact}) & asymptotic (\Cref{prop:asymptotic}) \\
\midrule
101 & $26 \times 26$ & 0.8938 & 0.9316 \\
1009 & $251 \times 251$ & 0.9229 & 0.9317 \\
2003 & $497 \times 497$ & 0.9259 & 0.9316 \\
10007 & $2478 \times 2478$ & 0.9296 & 0.9316 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Exact finite-$m$ value vs.\ asymptotic limit, four scales, $n/p \approx 0.495$ fixed. Both columns computed, every row: neither is a cited closed form.}
\label{tab:opi}
\end{table}

The exact value increases monotonically across all four scales, closing
roughly a third of the remaining gap with each $\sim 2\times$ increase in
$p$: the richer, operator-valued description at finite $m$ giving way to the
poorer scalar limit as $m$ grows, the same direction \Cref{thm:coreflector}
fixes abstractly, measured here rather than assumed. This does not stand
beside \cite{Jordan2024}'s own quantum-versus-classical comparison waiting
to be checked against it; it removes that comparison's premise.
\Cref{thm:generates} proves DQI's matrix is exactly the coreflector image
of the paraconsistent word's own ladder, so the mathematical content that
matrix computes was never reachable by anything beyond a classical
evaluation of the paraconsistent original in the first place: there is no
second, independently quantum object for a runtime race against Prange's
algorithm to be run between. Prange's algorithm appears in \Cref{tab:opi}
because it is how the source paper itself computes the classical decoding
step, not as one side of a contest this note stages.

\texttt{lagrange\_interpolate}, as written, is $\Theta(n^3)$ in the
interpolation degree, confirmed by timing ($n{=}500 \to 1.64$s/trial,
$n{=}992 \to 12.8$s/trial, a $7.8\times$ ratio matching $(992/500)^3=7.8$ to
the digit), not assumed from the code's shape. At $n\approx4954$
($p=10007$), one trial runs for tens of minutes, long enough that a fixed
trial count cannot bound wall-clock time; \texttt{opi run} now accepts a
wall-clock budget checked once per outer iteration of the interpolation
itself, catching an oversized trial in flight rather than only the gap
between trials. \Cref{lem:exact}'s eigenvalue solve never touches this loop
and ran to completion regardless, giving the $p=10007$ row above.

\section{Discussion}

\begin{figure}[h]
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}[
  node distance=9mm,
  box/.style={draw, rounded corners, align=center, inner sep=6pt, font=\small},
  arr/.style={-Stealth, thick}
]
\node[box] (fde) {Belnap/FDE register\\$\mathbf 4^{\odot m}$};
\node[box, below=of fde] (ladder) {IMASM ladder\\$S_+,\, S_-,\, D$};
\node[box, below=of ladder] (dqi) {DQI finite-$m$ operator\\$A^{(m,\ell,d)}$};
\node[box, below=of dqi] (eval) {$\lambda_{\max}(A)$\\$\langle s^{(m,\ell)} \rangle$};
\node[box, below=of eval] (asym) {$m\to p$ scalar limit\\$\frac12 + \sqrt{\frac{n}{2p}\left(1-\frac{n}{2p}\right)}$};

\draw[arr] (fde) -- node[right] {$\in,\, \ni,\, \top$} (ladder);
\draw[arr] (ladder) -- node[right] {coreflector, \Cref{thm:coreflector}} (dqi);
\draw[arr] (dqi) -- node[right] {$\lambda_{\max}$} (eval);
\draw[arr] (eval) -- node[right] {$m\to p$} (asym);
\end{tikzpicture}
\caption{One object traced through its paraconsistent, classical-logical,
and asymptotic descriptions. Each arrow is a proved step, not an analogy:
\Cref{thm:generates} for the first two, \Cref{lem:exact} for the third,
\Cref{prop:asymptotic} for the fourth.}
\label{fig:chain}
\end{figure}

The three legs of this note lock together (\Cref{fig:chain}).
\Cref{sec:collapse} proves, in
Lean, that the classical restriction of Belnap FOUR is reachable from either
side by a genuine adjunction, ex falso or ex quodlibet, and by nothing else.
\Cref{sec:word} constructs and mechanically verifies a
paraconsistent object of the class that claim is about, and
\Cref{thm:generates} identifies its own $\in$/$\ni$ ladder, term for term,
as \Cref{lem:exact}'s matrix $A$ under the ex-falso side of that collapse.
\Cref{sec:results}
measures, at four real scales, the classical shadow of that exact ladder
closing the gap to its own $m\to p$ limit, richer collapsing to poorer,
never the reverse. This is not three independent observations that happen
to point the same way: it is one object, its native ladder proven equal to
DQI's matrix, and that matrix's classical behavior measured directly.

The eigenvalue solve is $O(\ell)$ per power-iteration step and reaches
$\ell=2478$ in seconds regardless of $m$; the practical ceiling on pushing
\Cref{tab:opi} to larger $p$ is Prange's own interpolation step, not the
quantity this note is about. A shared-denominator or barycentric
reformulation of that interpolation would lift the ceiling and is the
natural next point on the curve.

\item \textbf{Theoretical:} the four files of \Cref{sec:collapse}
(\texttt{p4ramill/Imscribing/Paraconsistent/}): \texttt{ParaconsistentFrobeniusClosure.lean},
\texttt{DeMorganBooleanCentre.lean}, \texttt{ClassicalRestriction.lean},
\texttt{FalsifiabilityDegenerate.lean}, all \emph{sans} sorry.

\item \textbf{Empirical:} \texttt{mOMonadOS/src/opi.rs},
\texttt{G-mOMonadOS/src/opi.rs}, byte-identical, both run at the parameters
in \Cref{tab:opi}. Both columns of \Cref{tab:opi}, at every row, are output
from that same run; the asymptotic column is computed by \texttt{opi.rs}

1351	\section{Scholze--Stix and the vacuity produced by tensor-blind comparison}
1352	\label{sec:ss-vacuity}
1353	
1354	The Scholze--Stix objection must be stated at full strength.  Their analysis of
1355	the passage to IUT III, Corollary 3.12 argues that the $j^2$ factors attached to
1356	the concrete $\Theta$-pilot data cannot be retained while simultaneously making
1357	what they regard as consistent identifications among the ordered real lines in
1358	which the corresponding pilot quantities are represented.  Removing those
1359	factors yields an inequality of the form
1360	\[
1361	  0 \;\lesssim\; d(P),
1362	\]
1363	which they describe as essentially free of content; under the same
1364	simplifications, they remark that the relevant multiradial theorem becomes
1365	``not false, but trivial'' \cite{ss2018}.
1366	
1367	The tensor filtration does not answer this by introducing a quotient, a collapse,
1368	or a hidden identification.  There is no such operation.  The relevant object
1369	is a \emph{tensor filtration}.  The procession of tensor packets of log-shells
1370	is retained as a filtered object, and the weights occurring at different
1371	tensor positions are read at the positions at which they occur.  Schematically,
1372	write
1373	\[
1374	  0\subseteq F_0\mathcal T\subseteq F_1\mathcal T
1375	  \subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_m\mathcal T=\mathcal T
1376	\]
1377	for the tensor filtration of the common container.  What matters is not a
1378	single scalar line on which every $j$-label must act by the same normalization,
1379	but the tensor packet together with the filtration position at which each
1380	contribution occurs.  We may record that position by the filtration degree
1381	\[
1382	  \nu_F(x):=\min\{j:x\in F_j\mathcal T\}.
1383	\]
1384	Thus the $j^2$-weight is not an extra scalar inserted into one universal real
1385	line.  It is indexed by the position $j$ of the contribution in the tensor
1386	filtration:
1387	\[
1388	  \nu_F(x)=j
1389	  \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
1390	  \text{the corresponding $\Theta$-contribution carries weight }j^2.
1391	\]
1392	Different $j^2$-weights at different filtration positions do not constitute
1393	monodromy of one scalar line.  They are the filtration data.
1394	
1395	This is precisely why the Scholze--Stix scalar diagram and the IUT tensor
1396	calculation ask different questions.  Scholze--Stix require the various
1397	real-valued representatives to participate in one simultaneous system of
1398	identifications and then diagnose the $j^2$-dependence as an inconsistency in
1399	that system \cite{ss2018}.  But IUT III performs the multiradial representation
1400	on regions inside tensor packets of log-shells and only afterwards forms the
1401	log-volume of the resulting holomorphic hull \cite{iut3}.  The tensor packet is
1402	not decorative bookkeeping around an underlying one-dimensional comparison;
1403	it is where the comparison lives.

1590	\begin{proposition}[Filtered non-vacuity]
1591	Let $\mathcal T$ be a filtered tensor object and suppose a numerical estimate
1592	depends on weights $w_j$ carried at filtration positions $F_j\mathcal T$.  If
1593	one replaces the filtered readout by a readout that is insensitive to the
1594	filtration index $j$, then the resulting estimate may become tautological even
1595	though the filtered estimate is not.  The tautology of the tensor-blind readout
1596	does not imply the tautology of the filtered estimate.
1597	\end{proposition}

1599	\begin{proof}
1600	A $j$-insensitive readout factors all terms through data on which the distinction
1601	between $w_j$ and $w_k$ is unavailable.  Any contribution depending on that
1602	distinction is therefore absent from the resulting scalar expression.  No
1603	inverse inference from the scalar expression to the filtered expression is
1604	available unless the readout is proved faithful to the filtration.  Hence
1605	triviality after suppressing the filtration is compatible with nontriviality
1606	before that suppression.
1607	\end{proof}

1610	burden that a non-vacuous objection must meet.  To refute the IUT inequality on

1612	multiradial representation and show that the $j^2$-weighted information fails
1613	there.  Demonstrating that the inequality becomes empty after passing to a
1614	tensor-blind scalar comparison establishes the emptiness of that comparison.

1621	the differences that generate the estimate to disappear before they are
1622	measured.  In the language developed throughout this paper, the information is
1623	carried through the relation rather than normalized away prior to the readout.

1679	\section{Conclusion}
1680	
1681	The construction developed here is a rebased logical calculation, not a
1682	reinterpretation of a classical one.  Its continuous directed graph carries
1683	source, partition, branchwise transformation, information retention, fixation,
1684	fusion, carrier motion, phase, closure, and terminal readout.  Its carrier is
1685	\[
1686	\mathcal X=\mathcal P(\{T,F,t,f\}),
1687	\]
1688	with FOUR as a four-state slice and the Boolean pair $\{F,T\}$ as a further
1689	restriction.  Reflection and coreflection remove the nonclassical states in
1690	opposite directions, while the information closure retains contradiction at
1691	$B$.  Classicalization is therefore a loss operation performed after the richer
1692	state already exists.
1693	
1694	The four IUT papers move through this same mathematical structure.  The
1695	$\Theta$-link transports data between alien ring structures without identifying
1696	them as one ring.  The indeterminacies retain controlled multiplicity.  The
1697	log-$\Theta$ lattice carries several transport directions in one containment
1698	geometry.  Tensor filtration retains the positions of the $j^2$-weighted
1699	contributions through the multiradial calculation.  The terminal arithmetic
1700	statement is a bounded-discrepancy inequality produced after those operations,
1701	not a return to a Boolean foundation.
1702	
1703	The worked calculations make this concrete.  The engaging $\Theta$-link reaches
1704	\[
1705	A=\{T,F,t,f\}.
1706	\]
1707	The bounded-discrepancy graph satisfies its transformed reconnection predicate
1708	and terminates at
1709	\[
1710	Ftf=\{F,t,f\}.
1711	\]
1712	The cyclic shift $R$ leaves the structural predicates invariant while moving
1713	phase-bearing observables.  These are simultaneous properties of one directed
1714	graph and do not require resolution into a single classical pole.
1715	
1716	The Scholze--Stix vacuity result occurs only after the filtration position of the
1717	$j^2$ contribution no longer participates in the scalar comparison.  Inside the
1718	tensor filtration, that position remains part of the datum.  A vacuous
1719	position-insensitive scalar inequality therefore does not evaluate the filtered
1720	inequality from which the positional information was omitted.
1721	
1722	The resulting formulation uses ordinary maps, graph predicates, carrier states,
1723	cyclic actions, filtrations, and inequalities throughout.  Conventional
1724	notation does not classicalize the substrate: it is only the notation in which
1725	the rebased calculation is displayed.  Contradiction is
1726	retained without explosion, tensor position is retained without scalar
1727	flattening, and arithmetic readout occurs only after the complete graph
